sources.citation: Pstrusińska, Jadwiga. 2013. Secret Languages of Afghanistan and Their Speakers. Newcastle upon Tyne: Cambridge Scholars Publishing. ISBN 978-1-4438-4970-8. (30-page publisher sample: front matter, Introduction pp.1-16, start of ch.1)
sources.note: Nothing on stress. Introduction p.3 n.: Kieffer 1986:103 lists 'magatibai (with an annotation, "under research")' among Jat argots; p.10 n.23 cites Jasiewicz 1983: 87 on 'the Afghan Haydaris'; p.14: 'it would be of little value to attempt to introduce more precise phonological features into the argotic lexical material listed in the present work'. Chapter Four (pp.36-87), where Magati is treated, is not in the sample and was not accessible (Google Books API quota 0, search-inside 403).

sources.note: nothing; bibliographic record only (one reference in total, the 1986 wordlist note)

sources.citation: Pstrusińska, Jadwiga. 1986. Magati: some notes on an unknown language of northern Afghanistan. Journal of the Anthropological Society of Oxford 17(2): 135-139.
sources.note: Nothing on stress or accent anywhere in the 5 pages. The only linguistic data is a 31-item wordlist and 13 sentences gathered by Z. Jasiewicz and A. Ananicz in 1976, reproduced 'exactly as received (and transcribed, moreover, according to the rules of Polish orthography)' (p.136), with no stress marks; p.138: 'the grammatical system was very similar to that of a Persian dialect, whereas the vocabulary seemed to be of mixed origin'; p.136: speakers use 'Persian (in its local Dari version)' with outsiders and also know Uzbek. Open-access scan from Oxford ORA (scanned text layer).

sources.citation: Kieffer, Charles M. 1983 (updated 2011). AFGHANISTAN v. Languages. Encyclopaedia Iranica I/5: 501-516, section 32 (Jat argots).
sources.note: Nothing on stress. Says: 'Magatibai is the language of the Jōgī, who move about in the provinces of Balḵ, Jōzǰān, Fāryāb, and Kondūz. Part of its vocabulary is shared by Magadī of the Ḡorbat (see A. Rao, Note préliminaire sur les Jat d'Afghanistan, Studia Iranica 8, 1979, p. 144)'; the Jat argots are 'structurally Iranian'. Wayback capture../adur1234/ (live iranicaonline.org Cloudflare-blocked).
